message:
vc_obj2tifxyz: write scale as cells per voxel measured from the grid, fail on an empty grid

tifxyz "scale" counts grid cells per voxel: a tracer patch grown at step 20
stores 0.05, and vc_flatten, the Python reader and the upsampler all size
their output as extent * scale. vc_obj2tifxyz wrote the inverse in both the
UV-metric and the non-metric mode (OBJ units per cell, times mesh_units), so
a published segment converted with a stretch factor of 2000 carried
scale 0.0005 while its samples were 16.6 x 8.0 voxels apart. Downstream
vc_flatten then collapsed the 2001 x 2001 grid to a handful of cells (#1319).

Measure the spacing of the grid actually rasterized, after any decimation,
and store its reciprocal per axis. Source-scale mode (--tifxyz-source) still
adopts the input scale verbatim, so the VC3D flatten flow is unchanged.

With the default stretch factor an OBJ with UVs normalised to [0,1], the
parametrisation of every published segment mesh, produced a 2 x 2 grid with
no valid point and the tool still printed "Successfully converted" and exited
0 (#1320). Refuse to write in that case, exit non-zero, and explain that a
stretch factor or --uv-to-obj is needed. Fix the help text that called the
default invocation "legacy behavior".

Add an opt-in end-to-end test (VC_RUN_E2E=1) covering the empty grid, the
measured scale and the decimated scale on a synthetic normalised-UV mesh.

Fixes #1319
Fixes #1320

vc_obj2tifxyz: refuse 2 x 2 grids, reduce source scale by decimation, ignore mesh_units

The source-scale and mesh_units changes come from #1683 by Matteo
Bulloni, which took the same measured-spacing approach to #1319
earlier. The 2 x 2 refusal and the removal of the hint follow #1630 by
Anay.

With --tifxyz-source, the source scale was copied even when
--uv-downsample made the grid sparser. It is now
src_scale * (decimated_cols - 1) / (source_cols - 1) per axis, which
leaves it unchanged when nothing is decimated. The published
PHercParis4 tifxyz 20231007101619-on-20260310170716-45.532um (scale
0.05) was converted with vc_tifxyz2obj and back with --tifxyz-source
and --uv-downsample=4, which gives a 72 x 35 grid. The previous commit
wrote 0.05 (20 voxels per cell). This one writes 0.0125 (80 voxels per
cell). The measured spacing of adjacent samples is 77.5 x 75.1 voxels.
Without decimation both write 0.05, against a measured 19.9 x 19.5.
The --tifxyz-source help no longer says the output scale equals the
input scale.

mesh_units no longer divides the scale. The measured spacing is already
in voxels, so passing the Scroll 1 voxel size made the scale 7.91 times
too small: 20231007101619.obj with "2000 7.91" wrote 0.00760764,
0.0157312 (131.4 and 63.57 voxels per cell) against a measured spacing
of 16.61 x 8.03. It now writes 0.0601765, 0.124434, the same as
"2000 1.0". The argument is still accepted, and the help text says it
is not used for the scale. #1391 by Olga Ivanova had already kept
mesh_units out of the scale.

Any 2 x 2 output grid is now refused, not only an empty one. The tool
prints "Error: degenerate 2 x 2 output grid (N of 4 points rasterized);
refusing to write a tifxyz.", exits 1 and writes nothing. On #1630,
Matteo Bulloni reported a normalised-UV mesh that fills 1 of the 4
corners and slips past a zero-only check. As Anay put it there, a 2 x 2
grid is the clamped minimum, so it is degenerate whatever the user
passes. Real data shows the same: a fully valid 30 x 30 window (900 of
900 points) of the tifxyz above, exported with vc_tifxyz2obj
--normalize-uv and converted back at the default stretch, rasterizes 1
of 4 points. The previous commit wrote a 2 x 2 tifxyz with scale 1.0
and exited 0. This one exits 1 and writes nothing.

The Hint line after the empty-grid error is removed. It suggested a
stretch_factor and --uv-to-obj. --uv-to-obj never changes the grid
size, because the UV-metric grid is ceil(uv_range * stretch_factor) + 1,
and bruniss asked #1630 to stop recommending it and just report the
invalid output. The empty-grid error itself is unchanged. The help
note now says the tool exits non-zero when no grid point is rasterized
or the output grid is only 2 x 2, and the stretch_factor help says a
2 x 2 grid is refused.

lasagna/tifxyz_format.md takes #1683's wording for the definition of
scale and the resampling rule. It also drops the two bullets that
contradicted that definition (u = col * sx, and 1/sx as a
pixels-per-unit scaling), which #1683 and #1391 removed too.

test_obj2tifxyz_e2e gains five subcases and links vc_core to write the
source tifxyz with QuadSurface::save. The source-scale subcases with
and without decimation are the scenarios #1683's test covers, and the
mesh_units subcase covers the same check as #1391's final test. A 2 x 2
subcase converts a normalised 41 x 41 plane at the default stretch,
whose 2 x 2 grid is not empty, and expects a refusal. A stretch_factor
subcase checks that stretch 20 gives a 21 x 21 x.tif with scale 0.05
and stretch 80 gives 81 x 81 with 0.2, one of the tests
hendrikschilling asked for on #1391. Against the previous commit the
test fails 6 checks: 4 scale checks in the mesh_units and decimated
source-scale subcases, and 2 in the 2 x 2 subcase. Here it passes.
Most code comments added in the previous commit are removed, and two
older comments that called the source scale verbatim are fixed.

Refs #1319
Refs #1320

Co-authored-by: Matteo Bulloni <[email redacted]>
Co-authored-by: anay <[email redacted]>

test_obj2tifxyz_e2e: spawn the tool with an argument list

The test built one shell string from unquoted paths and handed it to
std::system, and it looked for the binary by splitting PATH on ':'.
Paths with spaces broke the command, and the separator is wrong on
Windows.

The tool is now started through QProcess with a QStringList, and the
only lookup is the VC_OBJ2TIFXYZ_BIN environment variable that the
ctest registration already sets to $<TARGET_FILE:vc_obj2tifxyz>. The
temporary root now contains spaces, so every subcase runs the tool on
such paths. A run that fails to start or does not exit normally is a
test failure instead of a non-zero code that a negative subcase could
mistake for the expected refusal. Qt6::Core is already required by the
test build.

vc_obj2tifxyz: reject non-default mesh_units with an explanatory error

The previous commit stopped multiplying the scale by mesh_units, which
is right for OBJs in base voxels, but it kept accepting an argument
documented as micrometers per OBJ unit without doing anything with it.
That leaves the coordinate contract implicit.

The tool now supports base-voxel OBJs only and says so. mesh_units is
deprecated: 1.0 is still accepted so existing invocations keep working,
and any other value exits 1 before the OBJ is read, with an error that
states that coordinates are expected in base voxels and are written
unchanged. The help text and the per-run log carry the same contract.
An explicit conversion from physical coordinates (--coords physical
with --obj-um-per-unit and --voxel-size-um) is left for a follow-up.

The e2e subcase that passed 7.91 now checks that 1.0 still writes the
measured scale and that 7.91 is rejected, writes nothing and names the
argument in the error.

test_obj2tifxyz_e2e: cover --uv-non-metric with decimation

Every subcase ran the default UV-metric mode, so the non-metric path,
whose written scale changed in 69a1c530b, had no end-to-end check.

A new subcase converts the normalised plane with --uv-non-metric, once
plain and once with --uv-downsample=2. It reads the emitted x/y/z.tif,
averages the distance between adjacent valid grid points along each
axis and checks that the reciprocals match the written scale. It also
pins the grid to 401 x 401 at scale 1.0 for both runs: in non-metric
mode decimation only thins the preliminary grid used to measure the
spacing, and the final grid is sized from the compensated measurement
either way, which for this mesh is one cell per OBJ unit. A wrong
compensation would change the grid even though the written scale
would still describe it.
